Having a relational database where you're charged purely for the calls you make is a game-changer. All of the relational databases I looked at in the past required a gateway node on at all times, which is far too expensive for a simple hobby project.
"We separated storage and compute" No. just no. Compute where the data lives, else you incur traffic cost and latency. A lesson learned in life, known from the dawn of time..

I am trying to understand how it works... the disk-backed storage here uses S3 which would introduce some severe latency... why would I run this over a local install if performance mattered at all to me?

I knew my bet to sticking with Postgres would pay off! This looks super exciting. Moving to Snowflake comes at the cost of losing so many Postgres features... I would be happy to pay 25x the price for a 10x speed increase.
I need some kind of pricing for me to consider this. Did I miss the page describing that?
Nice work Neon! I've used it a number of times and am impressed at how quickly databases become available. Leaps and bounds faster than RDS. it's amazing when you need something now.

For us that self-host, the architecture of building cold storage on top of Object Storage and warm storage on top of NVMEs is unbeatable. It enables us to build a much more cost-effective offering while keeping Postgres as our database.

Is 5 a reference to how you naked the prices so Neon doesn't work for light-workload, moderate storage databases anymore? $69+ a month for a Segment data warehouse holding 10gb is obnoxious. It was under $10 before the switch.
That probably works great for my use cases... Looking forward to seeing how this works out. I have no issues paying for services, I just hate that the minimum entry level cost is $20.
We use NeonDB in production and I the use of the term "branching" intuitive. We can branch off the main database to test things out, and periodically reset the branch to its parent.
I tried using supabase to back a vercel project. It was far too slow so we switched back to postgresql included with vercel. Turns out that was neon under the hood.

Is it feasible to use Neon connecting from smaller clouds, such as Hetzner, DO, Linode, etc?... For small workloads egress cost doesn't matter. For larger - well it does. I wish it was illegal to charge so much for egress for cloud providers.
What is a CPU? If it's AWS hosted for example it can range from a t2 (low end) to c7a (high end) and have huge performance impacts... It's weird that pricing is based on CPU but it's never defined.
